text:
St. Louis won this one by five goals, and the underlying numbers say that was a fair reflection of how it was played, even if the scoreboard exaggerated it. The Blues generated 3.44 expected goals to Ottawa's 1.81, outshot the Senators 54 attempts to 42, and won about 78 percent of simulated replays. They led the chance count in every period, which is why Ottawa never found a way to make this a one-goal game for long.

The early story was patience. Pius Suter's shorthanded snap shot at 14:28 of the first, a 14 percent look, gave the Blues the lead, and Jake Neighbours made it 2-0 in the second on a 3 percent wrister. Claude Giroux cut it to 2-1 with 8 seconds short of three minutes left in the period, but Mason McTavish answered 33 seconds later with a backhand, and that exchange was the real swing. Ottawa had a pulse for half a minute and then lost it.

The third period turned a comfortable win into a rout. Suter, Neighbours, McTavish on the power play and Adam Jiricek scored four times in a span of about nine minutes, with three of them coming in less than two minutes of play. Samuel Ersson allowed 7 goals on 3.44 expected, a gap of 3.56 goals that tells you the finish was harsher than the chances. Fabian Zetterlund's power-play goal late made it 7-2. McTavish and Suter each had two goals and an assist, and Neighbours added two goals.
